images.seen: Start map plausible: Rupert's Land, Qing with Tibet as vassal, Texas contested with Mexico, Cabanagem hatched in Brazil; Levant and Hejaz still Egyptian at 1 Jan as they should be.
End map plausible: Texas, California and New Mexico in the USA, Province of Canada, French Second Republic, Sikh Empire gone; nothing far outside its region.

Mexico holds West Texas and the Panhandle as plain Mexican land while the US keyframe also claims them (problem, patched as a contested ruling); US occupation hatching in California, New Mexico and the Nueces strip looks right.
Texas and the Cession are US; a pocket of nobody's land (68 cells, southern New Mexico and Arizona, the Gadsden strip) sits where Mexico's 1848 keyframe snap left it (left, not patched).
Egypt plus vassal Sudan, Ottoman Hejaz and Syria right in 1842; a tally of 1840-41 showed the Levant unowned and the Hejaz in Egyptian tint until the 1842 snap (patched).
India after the First Sikh War looks right: Sikh Empire reduced, Jammu and Kashmir a vassal, princely states in vassal tint, Mysore occupied; British Empire and East India Company share one colour.

Europe right (Schleswig contested, Hungary contested, Lombardy-Venetia, Galicia); one wrong hatch: Russian Bessarabia drawn as occupied by the Ottoman Empire, Moldavia itself not occupied by Russia (patched).
Russia holds Zhetysu (Almaty) and the East Kazakhstan edge from the Qing keyframe snap, six years before the page's 1854 annexation (patched).
West and Central Africa: many small dossier states, Sokoto and Kanem-Bornu with Bagirmi and Mandara cut out; nothing wrong that the pages could settle.
South America right: Riograndense Republic, Gobierno del Cerrito contested with Uruguay, Peru and Bolivia, Mapuche; no stray cells.
Mainland Southeast Asia right (Cambodia contested between Nguyen and Siam, Luang Phrabang, Chiang Mai as Siamese vassals); a few contested specks inside Siam, not worth a page.
West Texas now striped Mexico and United States for 1846-1847; the Nueces strip and New Mexico unchanged.
Syria and the Hejaz (Sharifate of Mecca in vassal tint) are Ottoman at the end of 1841, the same as 1842.

issues.what: Ottoman keyframe of 1840-1841 is Cliopatria's shape without Syria and the Hejaz (it restores them in 1842), so after the 27 Nov 1840 Convention the Levant (about 770 cells) was without an owner and the Hejaz (about 900 cells) stayed in Muhammad Ali's tint for 1840 and 1841, and the ledger's gain (muhammad-ali-dynasty/ledger/20, 21) was undone by the snap (917 cells removed in 1840, 2,416 added in 1842).

Qing keyframe of 1848-1852 loses 714 cells on the north-west steppe edge (Almaty/Zhetysu 475, East Kazakhstan 237) to Russia, marked unverified in the dossier; the pages date the Russian annexation of most of Zhetysu to 1854 and the large cession to 1864.

russian-empire/ledger/80 (Russia occupies Moldavia, April 1848, counterpart ottoman-empire) is compiled with roles reversed: its region 'Moldavia' covers Russian Bessarabia (the 130 cells of the Republic of Moldova plus), which Russia held, so 132 Russian cells were drawn as occupied by the Ottoman Empire from 1848 until 1851 (open relation), and Moldavia itself was not drawn occupied.

West Texas and the Panhandle (822 cells in 1846): both the US 1846 keyframe and Mexico's ledger claim them; the size rule gives them to Mexico as plain Mexican land. The pages show Mexico did not recognise Texas (it held the Nueces as the border) and the US held the Rio Grande claim until the 1848 cession, so the land is contested, not Mexican.

Kutai (sultanate-of-kutai-kartanegara_1842 keyframe, kutai-kingdom/ledger/5 and dutch-east-indies/ledger/46) use the place 'Muara Kaman', which the gazetteer lacks, so Kutai owns no land in 1842-1844 and the 1844 Dutch takeover is skipped; the same disc is given by the capital coordinates of the kutai-martadipura dossier (116.72 E, 0.2 S) in the patch. The dossier events themselves stay skipped.
danish-gold-coast_1849 keyframe names Keta (Ghana), which the gazetteer lacks, so the whole 1849 keyframe is unresolved (three small fort discs, the 1744 shape holds the colony meanwhile).

Mexico's 1848 keyframe snap removes 68 cells in southern New Mexico and Arizona (the Gadsden strip, Mexican until 1854) and the US ledger leaves them out, so they are nobody's land from 1848 on; fixing needs an exact line for the 1848 border, which I did not check against a page.

Emirate of Nejd is drawn about 4,200 cells (Najd plus all of Hasa and the Empty Quarter, from the Muhammad Ali loss region) in 1841-1845 against its own keyframe of 2,100 cells; the 1846 snap removes 2,635 cells of Eastern Province and Riyadh desert. The Emirate of Nejd page names Najd, Al-Ahsa, Qatif and Saihat and does not mention the Rub al-Khali or southern Arabia, so it gives no extent to correct the 1841-1845 years by.

Habesh Eyalet is drawn as an Egyptian colony (tint of muhammad-ali-dynasty) 1834-1864 by data/colonies.csv, but the page and the dossier's own ledger give Ottoman rule from 1827, Egyptian administration of Massawa and Suakin only 1846-1849, and the transfer to Egypt in 1866: about 764 cells of Red Sea coast carry the wrong tint in 1840-1845 and 1850-1864. A patch cannot close a colonies.csv relation.
issues.decision: left: pages silent (colonies.csv row, see problems)

issues.what: Size-rule conflicts of 300 cell-years and more, and the next ones: Taqali against Egypt in South Kordofan (Taqali is a vassal of the Turco-Egyptian Sudan and is drawn in its tint), Bhutan, Nepal, Sikkim, Manipur and the small states against the East India Company or British Empire, Bahawalpur against the Sikh Empire, Hunza and Nagar against Kashmir, Kengtung against the Qing, Dendi and Damagaram against Sokoto, the Herzegovina eyalet against the Ottoman Empire: the smaller state winning is what the dossiers and the pages for the period describe; no change.

Keyframe snaps of 200 cells and more other than the ones above (USA 1846 Oregon, USA and Mexico 1848 Texas, Afghanistan 1843, Republic of the Rio Grande 1840 and Centralist Mexico, Yucatan 1841, Brazil, Tripolitania 1840, Geledi 1843, French Algeria 1846, British Empire Baluchistan 1840-1842, East India Company Sind 1846): each follows an event in the dossiers or the contest that a ledger line covers; no change.

dossier_requests.what: ledger/46 (1844 gain of Kutai) and kutai-kingdom ledger/5 and keyframe sultanate-of-kutai-kartanegara_1842 name the place 'Muara Kaman' (Indonesia), which the gazetteer lacks; the patch carries the same land by coordinates (116.72 E, 0.2 S, 30 km), so the dossier events stay skipped. Add 'Muara Kaman' to places or give the dossiers a disc by coordinates.
dossier_requests.why: Unresolved regions in the packet; the same place is unresolved in earlier windows (kutai-kingdom 1635-1844 keyframes).

dossier_requests.what: Keyframe danish-gold-coast_1849 and ledger/15 use the place 'Keta' (Ghana), which the gazetteer lacks, so the 1849 keyframe is skipped; add 'Keta' to the places (the page used, Keta, Ghana, gives no coordinates) or give the fort discs by coordinates.

problems: colonies: data/colonies.csv row habesh-eyalet,muhammad-ali-dynasty,1834,1864 (confidence low) is wrong for 1834-1845 and 1850-1864: the page says 'it reverted to Ottoman rule in 1827', 'Massawa and Sawakin were given to him again in 1846, until his death in 1849' and 'In 1866 ... Habesh was taken away from Jeddah and formally incorporated into the Egyptian vice-kingdom'; the dossier's own ledger (rename 1827, 1846, 1849) says the same. About 764 cells of the Sudan and Eritrea coast are drawn in Egypt's tint in 1840-1845 and 1850-1864. Suggested rows: ottoman-empire 1557-1845, muhammad-ali-dynasty 1846-1849, ottoman-empire 1850-1865. Page https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habesh_Eyalet

boundary: events/2 of data/patches/p1840-p1849.json is dated 1851 (russian-empire occupation_end, principality-of-moldavia, April 1851): it closes the Moldavian occupation that events/1 opens in 1848; the dossier's own end (russian-empire/ledger/82, counterpart ottoman-empire) does not reach it. Applied with the note 'outside the window'; the p1850-p1859 agent must not duplicate it.

boundary: keyframe_overrides/1 replaces qing-dynasty_1848, whose years are 1848-1852, so the Qing keeps Zhetysu and the East Kazakhstan edge in 1850-1852 too (the pages say 1854 and 1864); Russia's keyframes of 1848 and 1849-1852 stay as they are and lose the conflict by the size rule, the Qing being smaller. The Qing keyframe of 1853-1855 (Cliopatria's smaller shape) belongs to p1850-p1859: it may need the same look, the page says Zhetysu was annexed in 1854.

boundary: keyframe_overrides/2 replaces sultanate-of-kutai-kartanegara_1842 (1842-1845); the previous keyframe sultanate-of-kutai-kartanegara_1734 (1734-1841) has the same Muara Kaman problem, so Kutai owns no land in 1840-1841; that is a matter for p1730-p1739 (first file wins), not patched here.

Left as drawn, noted for the next agent: the 1850 anchor holds the Ottoman occupation of Wallachia (267 cells, ledger/30) and a 6-cell leftover 'Ottoman land occupied by Russia' from russian-empire/ledger/81 (its 'Wallachia' region catches a few Ottoman-held Danube cells); both close in April 1851.

Minor dossier labels, not patchable: contest 'british-empire / gwalior-state' (war 'Second Anglo-Maratha War', 1843) duplicates 'gwalior-state / british-empire' (Gwalior campaign) with the war name of 1803-1805; contest argentine-confederation / paraguay is labelled 'Paraguayan War' (1864-1870) from 1838. Cell counts are 46 and 112.

Trial note: the stage compile differs from the published draft by other windows' and dossier edits made since 1 Nov (1,045 cells of the 1850 anchor, with an empty patch); the effect of this patch alone on the 1850 anchor (stage with the patch against stage with an empty patch) is 715 cells Russia to Qing, 132 cells of Russian Bessarabia no longer occupied, 138 Moldavian cells occupied by Russia, and a few single cells.
I looked at 13 images (11 before the patch, 2 after), three more than the 10 the brief suggests, and opened 9 pages of the 15.
